metadata.purpose: Evidence-backed disease/pest management knowledge for AI-assisted farmer advisory with mandatory Extension Officer supervision.

important_policy.recovery_is_dynamic: Recovery duration is not fixed. Each treatment case progresses through reassessment checkpoints until controlled, recovered, escalated, or referred.

update_notes: Added evidence-backed grape bacterial leaf spot protocol.
Added full tomato leaf mold cultural and weather-risk protocol.
Closed the two major evidence gaps from Version 1.
Chemical recommendations remain hidden pending officer and regulatory verification.

UCONN_TOMATO_LEAF_MOLD_2026.authority: University of Connecticut Integrated Pest Management
UCONN_TOMATO_LEAF_MOLD_2026.title: Tomato Leaf Mold
UCONN_TOMATO_LEAF_MOLD_2026.local_file: Tomato Leaf Mold _ Integrated Pest Management _ College of Agriculture, Health and Natural Resources _ University of Connecticut.pdf

immediate_actions: No disease-specific treatment required.
Continue regular crop monitoring.
Maintain good vineyard sanitation.
Continue appropriate irrigation, nutrition and canopy management.

monitoring: Inspect foliage, shoots and bunches for new lesions or fungal growth.
Increase observation frequency during weather favourable for grape diseases.

farm_visit_if: Symptoms appear despite healthy AI prediction.

symptoms: Irregular yellowish translucent spots on upper leaf surface.
White powdery/downy growth on lower surface.
Affected leaves become yellow, brown and dry.
Premature defoliation may occur.
Tender shoots may be dwarfed.
Berries may develop fungal growth, shrivel or develop soft rot.

immediate_actions: Flag affected vines for close monitoring.
Inspect neighbouring vines for similar symptoms.
Record recent rainfall and humidity.
Extension Officer should verify diagnosis before chemical intervention.

biological.details: ICAR reports need-based foliar application of Trichoderma afroharzianum together with soil drenching of Trichoderma asperelloides 5R can minimize downy mildew incidence.

monitoring: Reinspect newly emerging leaves and bunches.
Monitor closely following rainfall or prolonged high humidity.

laboratory_referral_if: Officer cannot distinguish downy mildew from similar disorders.

symptoms: Powdery growth mainly on upper leaf surface.
Malformation and discoloration of leaves.
Dark brown discoloration of stems.
Flower infection may cause shedding and poor fruit set.
Berry infection may cause shedding or cracking.

favorable_conditions.weather_description: Sultry warm conditions with dull cloudy weather are highly favourable.

immediate_actions: Inspect nearby vines and bunches.
Record disease extent and crop stage.
Flag severe berry or flower infection for officer review.

biological.details: ICAR reports alternating Trichoderma afroharzianum with sulphur reduced powdery mildew severity and fungicide applications.

chemical.recommendation_from_source: Inorganic sulphur 0.25%, chinomethionate 0.1%, or dinocap 0.05% are listed by the source.

monitoring: Monitor young leaves, shoots, flowers and berries.
Reassess progression after officer-approved intervention.

farm_visit_if: Flower or bunch infection is extensive.

symptoms: Minute water-soaked spots may appear on the lower leaf surface along major and lateral veins.
Spots may coalesce into larger patches.
Young growing shoots may be affected first.
Leaves, shoots and berries may become infected.
Berries may develop brownish-black lesions and later become small and shrivelled.
Necrotic or canker-like lesions may occur on shoots and petioles.

favorable_conditions.weather_risk_note: Warm, humid conditions within the source ranges are favourable for disease development.

immediate_actions: Mark affected vines for close observation.
Inspect nearby vines, young shoots and berries for similar water-soaked or dark lesions.
Avoid moving between visibly affected and healthy plants unnecessarily before sanitizing tools.
Collect photographic evidence from leaves, shoots and berries for Extension Officer review.
Record recent temperature, humidity and rainfall.

cultural.action: Collect and safely dispose of infected plant parts.
Maintain vineyard sanitation and sanitize tools used on symptomatic vines.

biological.evidence: Demonstrated inhibitory activity against Xanthomonas campestris pv. viticola under in-vitro conditions.
Demonstrated antagonistic potential against the pathogen under in-vitro conditions.

chemical.source_evidence: NHB source lists Streptocycline and copper/Bordeaux-based preventive treatments.
The ICAR-NRCG-linked research study tested several chemicals in vitro.

monitoring: Inspect newly emerging shoots and leaves.
Track whether lesions appear on additional vines.
Increase surveillance during warm and humid conditions.
Document whether berry symptoms appear.

crop_stage_rules.reason: Source indicates young growing shoots are affected first.

crop_stage_rules.action: Inspect berries for brown-black lesions and shrivelling.

schedule_farm_visit_if: Young shoots and berries are simultaneously affected.
The farmer cannot safely remove affected material.
laboratory_referral_if: Bacterial disease cannot be confirmed visually.
Symptoms overlap with fungal lesions or nutrient disorders.
A high-value vineyard has widespread symptoms.

immediate_actions: No disease-specific treatment required.
Continue disease and thrips scouting.
Maintain good field drainage.
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization.

monitoring: ICAR-DOGR IPM recommends field scouting for onion thrips and diseases twice weekly.

symptoms: Small white sunken spots develop initially.
Lesions enlarge and become eye-shaped under moist conditions.
Lesions become purple with broad chlorotic margins.
Severe infection may affect neck and bulb tissue.

immediate_actions: Assess affected area and crop age.
Improve drainage where water is accumulating.
Check for simultaneous thrips pressure.
Extension Officer reviews proposed intervention.
cultural: Use recommended fertilizer doses and avoid excessive nitrogen.

biological.details: Trichoderma viride is included in the national IPM recommendations; ICAR-DOGR also includes Trichoderma seed and field application in onion IPM.

chemical.recommendation_from_source: National vegetable IPM source lists Mancozeb, Chlorothalonil and Iprodione schedules.

monitoring: Twice-weekly disease scouting under ICAR-DOGR IPM.
Record lesion expansion and percentage of affected foliage.

crop_stage_rules.note: ICAR-DOGR identifies this as a peak foliar-disease management period.

laboratory_referral_if: Purple Blotch and Stemphylium cannot be differentiated.

symptoms: Symptoms may appear from the 3-4 leaf stage.
Small yellow to orange flecks or streaks appear.
Lesions become elongated or spindle-shaped.
Spots may coalesce and blight large portions of foliage.

favorable_conditions.seasonal_note: National IPM source reports greater severity in rabi and during higher temperatures in March-April.

immediate_actions: Remove or isolate heavily affected crop refuse where practical.
Assess drainage and plant density.
Request officer confirmation because mixed infection with Purple Blotch may occur.
cultural: Field sanitation and destruction of infected crop refuse.

chemical.recommendation_from_source: Three to four sprays of Mancozeb 0.25% at 20-day intervals starting 60 days after transplanting are described in the source.

monitoring: Twice-weekly scouting is recommended in ICAR-DOGR onion IPM.
Track percentage foliage affected.

crop_stage_rules.action: Source-based treatment window begins if treatment is required and approved.

laboratory_referral_if: Disease identity remains uncertain after officer review.

immediate_actions: No disease/pest-specific treatment required.
Continue pest and disease monitoring.
Maintain balanced fertilizer and irrigation practices.

monitoring: Regular pest monitoring.
Assess biocontrol potential approximately every 10 days.
Maintain pheromone traps where bollworm surveillance is required.

immediate_actions: Record affected area.
Inspect for crop residue-associated disease pressure.
Increase surveillance during humid and rainy periods.
cultural: Remove and destroy infected plant residues.

chemical.recommendation_from_source: TNAU lists multiple fungicide options and treatment points at 60, 90 and 120 DAS.
ICAR AICRP reports Dithane M-45 or copper oxychloride as two foliar sprays at 10-day interval.

crop_stage_rules.action: TNAU source identifies these as treatment/biological-control checkpoints.

immediate_actions: Inspect adjacent plants.
Record spread and recent rainfall/irrigation.
Officer verification required before bactericide recommendation.

biological.details: ICAR AICRP reports Flavobacterium and Pseudomonas fluorescens as effective against cotton bacterial blight.

chemical.recommendation_from_source: ICAR AICRP reports streptocycline 100 ppm + copper oxychloride 0.3% as foliar spray at 10-day interval.

monitoring: Reassess lesion expansion before repeating any intervention.

immediate_actions: Inspect squares, flowers and bolls for larvae and feeding damage.
Check pheromone-trap activity.
Do not assume Pink Bollworm species from Model 1 alone.
Extension Officer should identify the bollworm species where possible.
cultural: Use appropriate intercrops/trap crops where locally suitable.
Hand collect and destroy larvae and damaged plant parts where feasible.

biological.details: ICAR reports use of Trichogramma, neem and NPV during early crop growth as components of cotton IPM.
Cotton IPM encourages biological-control fauna and need-based action rather than automatic spraying.

monitoring: Assess pest population approximately every 10 days.
Use pheromone traps for bollworm monitoring.
Use scouting and economic-threshold-based action.
Record crop stage and damaged fruiting structures.

actions: Extension Officer determines whether threshold-based intervention is justified.

laboratory_referral_if: Species confirmation is essential for management decisions.

immediate_actions: No disease-specific treatment required.
Continue crop scouting.
Maintain field sanitation.
Avoid unnecessary pesticide application.

monitoring: Watch lower foliage for Early Blight symptoms.
Increase surveillance during prolonged humid/cloudy conditions.

symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings.
Yellow margins may surround lesions.
Symptoms may occur on leaves, stems and fruits.

immediate_actions: Inspect lower leaves and surrounding plants.
Remove heavily infected lower plant debris where appropriate.
Assess canopy humidity and airflow.
cultural: Use healthy seed from disease-free fruits.
Reduce relative humidity within the canopy.

chemical.recommendation_from_source: National vegetable IPM source describes two chlorothalonil 0.2% sprays at an 8-day interval, starting soon after infection on floral parts.

monitoring: Reassess after the first management checkpoint.
Track appearance of new lesions rather than expecting old lesions to disappear.

symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions on leaves and stems.
Lesions may expand rapidly.
White sporulation may appear.
Fruit may develop dark lesions and soft rot.

favorable_conditions.weather_description: Moist/cloudy conditions favour disease expression; the IPM source specifically discusses cold, cloudy and drizzling weather.

immediate_actions: Treat as high-priority because disease may spread rapidly.
Inspect surrounding plants immediately.
Remove infected debris/fruits according to officer guidance.
Record current rainfall, humidity and cloud conditions.
cultural: Use healthy certified seed from disease-free areas.
Remove infected crop debris and fruits.
Use staking to reduce Phytophthora disease pressure.

chemical.recommendation_from_source: Preventive Mancozeb 0.25% sprays are described during cloudy, cold and drizzling weather.
One Metalaxyl + Mancozeb 0.2% treatment is described when applied within two days of infection. The source explicitly states repetitive sprays should not be given.

monitoring: Short-interval reassessment because late blight may progress rapidly.
Monitor weather risk and new lesion development.

symptoms: Older/lower leaves are commonly affected first.
Pale green to yellow spots develop on the upper leaf surface.
Olive-green to brown velvety fungal growth develops on the corresponding lower leaf surface.
Lesions may enlarge, turn brown and become necrotic.
Severely infected leaves may wither, die or drop.
In severe disease, blossoms and fruit may also be affected.

immediate_actions: Inspect the lower surface of older leaves for olive-green or brown velvety growth.
Reduce avoidable leaf wetness.
Avoid overhead irrigation where practical.
Increase airflow around plants.
Separate or mark heavily symptomatic plants for Extension Officer assessment.
Photograph both upper and lower surfaces of leaves.

cultural.action: Use drip irrigation and avoid wetting foliage.
Space plants adequately to improve airflow.
Stake, trellis or prune appropriately to increase airflow around foliage.
Remove and dispose of infected plant material.
Sanitize tools, stakes, trellises and equipment that contacted infected plants.
Remove crop residue after the production cycle.
Use clean seed from a reputable source.

chemical.source_note: UMN and Cornell discuss fungicide options for their jurisdictions.
chemical.important_note: Foreign extension pesticide recommendations must not be directly transferred to Indian use.

monitoring: Increase scouting when RH approaches or exceeds 85%.
Inspect older/lower leaves first.
Photograph both leaf surfaces during follow-up.
Track whether new lesions appear after humidity reduction.
Reassess within approximately 7 days for active cases.
Be aware that under favorable conditions new spores may form within roughly 10-12 days.

crop_stage_rules.action: Maintain airflow and humidity control throughout crop growth.
Escalate officer review if blossoms or fruits show symptoms because severe disease can affect them.

actions: flag active cases for closer follow-up

schedule_farm_visit_if: Disease is spreading despite humidity and sanitation measures.
Large areas of crop are affected.
laboratory_referral_if: Leaf Mold cannot be differentiated from another foliar disease.
Management response is poor despite verified diagnosis.
